headline: Wall Street erased most of a deep AI-led sell-off on Wednesday, then shut for Thanksgiving, with a hot inflation print locking in bets on a December Fed hike.
numbers_note: Only the intraday swing passed the filter: a 3%+ drop in the S&P 500 that reversed to -0.25% is a big reversal, while the closing moves, the 3bp drop in the 10-year and WTI's 2% gain were all inside the filter.

points.text: The S&P 500 fell as much as 3.2% and the Nasdaq as much as 4.6% on Wednesday before recovering; the S&P closed down 0.25% at 7,182.78, the Nasdaq down 0.62% at 23,585.80, and the Dow up 0.33% at 50,182.95. CNBC said no specific catalyst for the bounce could be pinpointed, though traders cited light pre-holiday trading and a Michael Burry blog post.
Tech fell as the lift from Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO faded and failed to calm worries about whether the AI trade can last.

October PCE inflation rose to 3.8% a year from 3.7%, and core PCE was 3.3%, slightly above the 3.2% forecast. Yet the 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 3bp to about 4.87% as investors bought bonds for protection.
Hotter core inflation, an upward revision to Q3 GDP and a Fed survey showing sticky inflation cemented expectations of a 25bp Fed hike in December and another in early 2027.
The White House proposed new 'overcapacity' tariffs on 14 trading partners including China, the EU and India; officials say they are months away from taking effect.

drivers.text: AI rebound: at 08:47 ET Nasdaq futures were up about 2%, S&P 500 futures up 1.4% and Dow futures up 1.2%, with Nvidia up over 3% premarket as AI-linked stocks recovered. Kospi rose 4.3% on memory chips. Gold futures rose 3.6% to about US$3,660 and silver jumped over 9%. If gains hold, all three indexes finish the week up more than 4%; the Nasdaq is still more than 14% below its peak.

Rates are not helping: the 10-year Treasury yield rose more than 5.5bp to above 4.90% and the 2-year moved toward 4.70%. Markets price a 99% chance of a 25bp December hike (LSEG). The Fed's pre-meeting blackout starts Saturday.

Opening shape: futures pointed to a gap up of roughly 1–2% vs Wednesday's close. Whether the first 15 minutes extended or faded that move is not confirmed. Equities rising while yields rise means the rally is a positioning bounce in AI names, not a rates relief trade.

us_open.for_tomorrow: Bursa and most of Asia are shut for the weekend, so the next read-through is Monday's open. If this rebound holds into the close, Asian tech and Bursa data-centre names get a positive lead, but Kospi's 4.3% jump shows Asia has already priced much of it. US yields rising toward 4.90% with a December hike locked in still works against the ringgit. On a thin half-day, treat the equity move as low-conviction.

us_open.setup: The US is set to open sharply higher in a thin post-Thanksgiving half-day as battered AI and chip stocks rebound, even as Treasury yields rise with a December Fed hike fully priced.

watch.event: Early cash close (13:00 ET) on thin volume
watch.why: A close near the highs with the Nasdaq still up about 2% would confirm the AI rebound. Giving back most of the gain would show it was holiday-light buying, like Wednesday's intraday swing.

watch.event: Fed blackout begins ahead of the December meeting
watch.why: Fed speakers go quiet after this, so the 99% hike pricing stands as is. Any late Fed comment before then that cools hike talk would ease yields. Hawkish comments would keep the 10-year above 4.90%.
